findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:205 `span : ∀ v : V, ∃ a b c₁ c₂ : ℝ, v = a • pTransverse g K + b • K.q + c₁ • e₁ + c₂ • e₂` (so dim V ≤ 4); ParityOdd.lean:335-339 `eq_zero_of_isLorentzCovariant` already takes `hspan`/`hnull` free-form instead of a plane, and ParityOdd.lean:223 `exists_halfTurn` uses only `e₁`,`e₂` orthogonality and non-nullity — never `span`.
findings.fix: Restate the four lemmas from dimension-free hypotheses in the style the same file already uses at line 335 — `hspan : ∀ v, ∃ a b u, g K.q u = 0 ∧ g (pTransverse g K) u = 0 ∧ v = a • pTransverse g K + b • K.q + u` plus a partner hypothesis `∀ u, g K.q u = 0 → g (pTransverse g K) u = 0 → u ≠ 0 → g u u ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ u', g K.q u' = 0 ∧ g (pTransverse g K) u' = 0 ∧ g u u' = 0 ∧ g u' u' ≠ 0` — and derive the `SpectatorPlane` versions from them; alternatively make `∀ v, W K.p v = 0` a field of `ParityOddAssumptions` per roadmap convention 6.
findings.issue: `apply_pTransverse_eq_zero` (274), `apply_p_eq_zero` (281), `apply_pTransverse_eq_zero_right` (290) and `apply_p_eq_zero_right` (296) all take `hP : SpectatorPlane g K`, i.e. the four-dimensionality input (`SpectatorPlane.span` forces `V = span{p_T, q, e₁, e₂}`), for conclusions that do not need it. `W p_T u = 0` for a spectator `u` needs only a half-turn `reflect u ∘ reflect u'` in `u` and one orthogonal non-null spectator partner `u'` (plus a `SpectatorAssumptions.span`-style decomposition of `v`), which holds for a definite spectator subspace of any dimension ≥ 2. The roadmap names exactly this as the trap to avoid: "forcing every statement about `F₃` to carry a four-dimensionality hypothesis that only one theorem actually needs" (InclusiveStructureFunctions/README.md convention 6), and it lists annihilation of `p` among the properties `A` carries, not a consequence of the plane.

findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:120-123 and Basic.lean:393-399 contain the same three-step argument; the PR already factored the other shared step this way (`covariant_spectator_apply_eq_zero`, Basic.lean:630, used from both files).
findings.fix: State the general lemma once, e.g. in `Bilin`/`Hadronic` in Basic: `lemma apply_eq_zero_of_apply_eq_self_of_apply_eq_neg {W : Bilin V} {f : V →ₗ[ℝ] V} (hf : ∀ v w, W (f v) (f w) = W v w) {v u : V} (hfv : f v = v) (hfu : f u = -u) : W v u = 0`, then get `covariant_spectator_offDiagonal_zero` by instantiating at `Bilin.reflect g u` and the ParityOdd use by instantiating at `hW f hf hdet`.
findings.issue: `IsProperLorentzCovariant.apply_eq_zero_of_apply_eq_self_of_apply_eq_neg` re-proves, for the proper-covariance predicate, the argument already proved for the full one in `Tensors/Basic.lean:390` (`covariant_spectator_offDiagonal_zero`, lines 395-399: rewrite `f u = -u`, `map_neg`, `linarith`). Neither `IsKinematicStabilizer` nor `det f = 1` enters the argument; they only serve to feed `hW`, so the lemma is a special case of a predicate-free statement and the two covariance notions cannot share it as written.

summary: The headline uniqueness results sit at the right level, but the four `annihilates p / p_T` corollaries carry the four-dimensionality input they do not need, and the sign-flip core of covariance is now proved twice, once per covariance predicate.
